decision_authority.policy: MRX continuous quality-gated publication and two-image article creative directive

title: How Much Are Mineral Rights Worth: Due Diligence In 2026
findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is f82ebccdf3823d720b58c011e44476e500939c420fca33409b23081d2ac51052; all 7 declared official sources passed live access review.

MRX methodology claims remain bounded to its current first-party page; RRC claims remain bounded to reported-production lag, corrections, query scope, cadence, and permit-status evidence; Texas State Library claims remain bounded to record location; EIA claims remain bounded to forecast vintage and revision context.

The article uses no fabricated owners, deeds, wells, permits, production, payments, prices, forecasts, acreage, ownership decimals, valuation ranges, testimonials, or owner-specific title, legal, tax, accounting, engineering, investment, reserve, or valuation conclusions.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Published DCF Methodology (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX methodology identifies production history, decline context, operator evidence, royalty terms, commodity assumptions, discount rate, title and acreage, and any offer terms as dated inputs to a directional range with assumptions stated.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the methodology only to define which inputs need an effective date, source, and refresh note; it does not rebuild the DCF, certify a value, prove title or reserves, guarantee an outcome, or recommend a transaction.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Production Data (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission of Texas production-data page identifies compilations, monthly ledgers, queries, and downloads built from production information reported to the Commission by Texas operators.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses that page to identify a current official source class and observation date for reported production only; it does not treat reported production as title, owner-decimal, payment, reserve, future-production, or value proof.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Production Data Query System FAQs (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The RRC production FAQ states that Texas production is reported by lease, online information has a two-month lag, operator reports can later be revised, corrected, or submitted delinquently, and historical records become substantially complete only after time passes.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses those statements to require an observed-through date, source-update date, and correction note; it does not infer a specific well allocation, title, payment entitlement, reserves, future production, or value.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Online Research Queries (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The RRC research-query directory provides official query routes for production, drilling permits, well records, and related records and states update cadences for several query systems, including nightly updates for completions and drilling permits.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses those cadences to distinguish a query date from an underlying event or filing date; it does not claim that a current query proves drilling, completion, production, ownership, or value.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Drilling Permit W-1 Query (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The official RRC drilling-permit query exposes filters for permit status, operator, lease, well, field, location, submitted date, and approved date, and identifies returned records by the selected query criteria.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the query as one dated development-evidence source and requires status and query date to remain visible; it does not equate an application or approved permit with a drilled, completed, producing, or economically successful well.

sources_inspected.label: Texas State Library, Land and Property History Research (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas State Library explains that deeds, surveys, liens, tax records, and ownership transfers are maintained by the county where the property is located and that county availability and older-record handling differ.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses that guidance to identify the county-record source class and access date; it does not claim that an online search is exhaustive or that one record resolves chain of title, reservations, legal effect, or owner-specific ownership.

sources_inspected.label: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Short-Term Energy Outlook (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook displays its release date, forecast-completion date, next release date, current assumptions, and changes from the prior monthly forecast.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses that current federal forecast only to demonstrate why commodity assumptions need a named source and vintage; it does not import a price into an owner-specific model, predict a property outcome, guarantee a forecast, or replace the review benchmark actually used.
